items.scene: Maya saves money each week so she can buy a laptop for her design course.
items.question: Which goal is higher-level in Maya's goal structure?
options: Buying a laptop for her design course is the higher-level goal; saving money is a subordinate goal.
Saving money each week is the higher-level goal; buying a laptop is a local step.
Both goals are unrelated because they happen at different times.
The higher-level goal is whichever one Maya chooses first.
items.why_this_case_matters: This is a direct means-end hierarchy: saving money serves the broader goal of buying the laptop.

items.scene: Leo wants to go jogging, but he also wants to stay home and finish a movie. He has only one free hour.
items.question: Which goal will Leo choose?
options: Jogging is higher-level because it is healthier.
Finishing the movie is higher-level because it is more relaxing.
This asks for a choice between goals, not a goal hierarchy.
Both goals are local steps toward the same larger aim.
items.why_this_case_matters: The scene has competing goals and asks for selection, so it should not be handled as goal hierarchy.

items.scene: Nina opens the app to check the bus schedule so she can arrive at the interview on time.
items.question: How should the goals be classified?
options: Opening the app is the superordinate goal; arriving on time is a local step.
Checking the bus schedule is a local or short-term goal serving the higher-level goal of arriving on time.
Arriving on time is lower-level because it happens after checking the schedule.
The first mentioned goal must be the higher-level goal.
items.why_this_case_matters: This tests the shortcut of treating the earlier or first-mentioned action as higher-level.

items.scene: Sara promised to help her brother move, but she also wants to attend a concert that starts at the same time.
items.question: Which goal is more important to Sara?
options: Helping her brother is subordinate to attending the concert.
Attending the concert is subordinate to helping her brother.
This is about importance or priority between conflicting goals, not nesting.
Both are local steps toward the same stated long-term goal.
items.why_this_case_matters: The question asks about priority in a conflict, which is outside the unit's scope.
